Running TreeHacks 2026 was one of the best highlights of my senior year at Stanford! In April 2025, I found out I would become the first female CFO in TreeHacks’ 12-year history. I remember sitting with that news for a moment, realizing the excitement and responsibility that came with the position. Behind the scenes, TreeHacks is months of meticulous budgeting, sponsor strategy, risk planning, and thousands of small decisions that nobody sees, all to make 36 hours of magic feel effortless. Some highlights: $500K+ in prizes ~1,000 hackers flown in from around the world Dozens of sponsors and industry partners, such as OpenAI , Anthropic , NVIDIA , and more Guest speakers including Sam Altman, Ali Partovi , Garry Tan , David Holz and more As a senior, it would have been easy to coast. Instead, I chose to have fun with a brilliant team of 27 ambitious students to put together one of the largest collegiate hackathons in the world. I want to especially give a huge shoutout to the officer team for all of the impressive work they've done and for making this event possible Thijs Simonian , Hannah Gao , Rachel Fernandez , Nathalie Ayala , Hannah T. Shu ! Onto the next adventure! 💚 ...more ...more

My journey as a TreeHacks organizer has come to an end. *cue crying hamster video* Serving as Social and Marketing Chair reshaped how I think about building products and brands. For the past two years, I went deep into short-form hype videos to build traction for TreeHacks. We amassed millions of views and increased following count. Studying hooks and retention taught me how attention is earned. Throughout this weekend during TreeHacks, I walked around during the judging period and realized that the difference between a good project and a winning project is not just technical depth. It is the marketing. The teams that win know how to frame the problem, communicate impact clearly, and make judges believe in the vision. They do not just ship features. They sell the belief. That skill translates directly into startups and any company. We as consumers will always flow to the clearest and boldest story. A strong narrative can accelerate any product. I am walking away convinced that marketing is not silly little job. It is one of the most crucial skills any builder needs and it should be more highlighted in industry. I am incredibly grateful for my two years as a TreeHacks organizer and being part of this wonderful and exciting family. Thank you to Rachel Fernandez , Hannah Gao , Thijs Simonian , Christina D. , and my wonderful co social chair Nathalie Ayala for being the best officer team I possibly could have asked for. Thank you to our saplings this year and last year's organizing team 💚💚💚 On to my next adventure! #TreeHacks #Marketing #Leadership ...more ...more

Building off Yair K. 's post: https://lnkd.in/gxqV3Wjx Proud of what our team built at Stanford University 's TreeHacks 2026 this weekend. Working with Anton Lee and Yair K. , we developed Tempo — a 4D Volumetric Telepresence & Chrono-Spatial Memory System, shortlisted for the Grand Prize. I focused on the real-time volumetric capture, calibration, streaming, and collaborative systems stack: • Designed a distributed multi-sensor fusion pipeline with C++ Kinect v2 sensor clients and a C# orchestration server over a custom TCP binary protocol (length-prefixed framing, sub-frame synchronization) • Implemented marker-based extrinsic calibration using OpenCV solvePnP with median filtering and outlier rejection, computing stable world transforms across sensors • Integrated optional ICP-based registration refinement via native C++ DLL • Built an OpenGL (OpenTK) renderer using interleaved VBOs for dense point cloud visualization, annotations, skeleton overlays, and camera/marker gizmos • Engineered a compact 9-byte/vertex wire format (quantized XYZ + RGB) enabling ~50% bandwidth reduction and sustained ~30 FPS streaming • Developed multi-server TCP/WebSocket networking (sensor ingestion, local transfer, web bridge, remote viewer) with robust TCP fragmentation handling and dead-client pruning Key system features: • Collaborative shared annotations: multi-client point / circle / polyline tools with JSON sync protocol, atomic ReplaceAll updates, per-author tracking • Live multi-viewpoint telepresence: bidirectional camera state replication allowing any connected client to drive the shared 6-DoF viewpoint • Instant 30-second rollback (“shadow replay”): 900-frame ring buffer with async frame delivery and variable playback speed • Snapshot vs live diff visualization: dual-viewport OpenGL viewer overlaying point clouds for Git-style spatial comparison • Random-access volumetric replay: custom binary formats (.lsreplay / .lssnap) with frame offset tables and embedded annotation metadata Systems engineering highlights: • Managed synchronization across 10+ concurrent threads with granular locking and non-blocking client management • Eliminated GC stalls in C++/C# interop via buffer pooling and atomic reference swaps • Implemented desynchronization detection, sanity limits, and drain-and-reconnect recovery paths Seeing live, navigable 3D memories streamed across desktop, web, and HoloLens 2 was an incredible moment. We won at TreeHacks 2026 by building GridVeda. Here's the story: One week ago, my team did not even know each other. We were a random assortment of four freshmen Stanford University , University of California, Berkeley , and Harvard who connected through a mutual friend just days before arriving at TreeHacks . Although we had no previous hackathon experience, our motley band decided to spend our thirty six hour weekend tackling massive challenges facing our national energy infrastructure. Having grown up in Maryland, California, and Oregon, we have all witnessed how fragile power grids can be. We have seen wildfires in the West and severe storms on the East Coast leave communities out to die in the dark for days. Because nearly half of the distribution infrastructure in the United States is currently at the end of its useful life, we envisioned a tool that moves us away from reacting to blackouts and toward predicting them instead. Thus, enduring back-to-back sleepless nights, we developed an intelligence system for electrical transformers that operates entirely without a cloud connection, perfect for grid tools that must remain functional during the same storms that frequently disable the internet. We combined a six qubit variational quantum circuit with classical ensembles to reach a fault classification accuracy of 98.09%. By utilizing Nemotron and cuQuantum on NVIDIA hardware, we enabled diagnostics that occur in less than one second. Additionally, we built a system to analyze incident reports and map that data onto three dimensional models to show exactly where a failure is brewing. After a weekend of hard work and becoming visibly fried, we finally won the Sustainability Track with the Best Prototyping Process. I am profoundly grateful to my teammates Shreyan Paliwal , Rehaan Kadhar , and Neil Chandran for their incredible dedication during the whole weekend as well as the team behind the Stanford EcoPreneurship ( Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability ) Sustainability Track. We also want to thank the sponsors and organizers at TreeHacks Team for providing the opportunity that made this possible. Excited to have won 2nd place in the OpenAI Artificial Intelligence Track at TreeHacks 2026 with my amazing teammates Maanit Goel , Nathan Zhou , and Grace Yan ! We built ContainOS, a physics-grounded multi-AI agent co-pilot that provides real-time decision support to firefighters during the critical first hours of wildfire containment. Our platform ingests data about the fire perimeter, wind speeds, terrain, and historical fires to continuously generate prioritized alerts on where the fire is headed, which towns are at risk, and the single best action for containment. Under the hood, we combined a physics engine to compute fire spread predictions, Gemini to analyze historical fires, ChatGPT agents to produce tactical recommendations, and a validator to ensure that AI outputs are physically possible. Throughout the 36 hours, we iterated directly with former CalFire chief Jake Hess to make sure we were building exactly what an incident commander would use in the field. We even integrated with The Interaction Company of California ’s Poke for real-time text updates! Can’t think of a better way to spend Valentine’s Day weekend! 💗 ...more ...more

We went to Stanford University and won Google’s AI track at TreeHacks 🏆 This weekend, my team, Spandan Patel , Ekagra Gupta , and I built Clarifyd, a classroom support tool for students with disabilities. Our goal? Provide teachers and students with immediate help, without waiting through lengthy school licensing and accommodations workflows. But honestly, the win was a small part of it. TreeHacks was unreal. 1,098 participants and $606,605 in cash on the line. Sam Altman, Garry Tan, and Ali Partovi opened, and afterwards it was straight to building. We pulled an all-nighter, took a 1am poker break to reset our brains, then went right back to debugging before demos and judging. And somehow, everything came together at the end. I did all of it on basically no sleep. Left Chicago at 3am for my flight out, got back at 7am, then had a midterm that afternoon. Worth it. Big thanks to Benedict (couldn’t find your LinkedIn), Michelle Vinocour , Anson Omar , and the whole TreeHacks team for running a great event and taking care of everyone all weekend! On to the next one 🚀 #Stanford #Treehacks #Google #Hackathon ...more ...more

So much fun this Sunday morning at TreeHacks at the project show. Congratulations to all the hackers and to the organizing students: it is an amazing production that takes huge effort to put together. One of the projects I saw was personal to me as my dad is blind. Team Shepherd ( Arjun Oberoi , Shane Mion , Tony Wang , Anthony Chukhlov ) built a smart cane to help the 40M blind people worldwide walk without bumping into things. 💚 Shepherd is a motorized smart cane that uses iPhone LiDAR and computer vision to detect obstacles and physically guide the user away from them in real time, and is also able to navigate users using GPS with an interactive voice interface. It was great to run into Vivian Z. , my student at Lean Launchpad last year, who was part of Team Mira Mira, who built an AI powered smart mirror that helps you decide what to wear. ...more ...more
